healthcareSystem: Government healthcare free for citizens; tourists use private hospitals or pay at public facilities. Quality care in Muscat.
qualityNotes: Good quality healthcare in Muscat with modern private hospitals. Public hospitals adequate but can be crowded. Very limited healthcare outside Muscat and Salalah — remote desert and mountain areas have minimal facilities.
pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies open 8am-10pm. Limited 24/7 options outside Muscat. Pharmacies close during Friday prayer.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Muscat are well-stocked. Pharmacists generally speak English. Outside Muscat, pharmacy availability is limited. Stock up on medications before desert excursions or trips to remote areas.
prescriptionRules: Prescription required for most medications. Oman has strict drug control laws similar to other Gulf states. Foreign prescriptions generally not accepted — need Omani doctor's prescription.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: All codeine products are prohibited in Oman.

restrictedMeds.name: Amphetamines (Adderall, Vyvanse)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly prohibited. Severe criminal penalties for possession.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis/CBD products
restrictedMeds.note: Zero tolerance. Severe penalties including imprisonment.

restrictedMeds.name: Psychotropic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Requires documentation from prescribing physician and approval from Omani authorities.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter in English listing all medications with generic names. Keep medications in original packaging. For controlled substances, obtain prior approval from the Oman Ministry of Health. Bring no more than 3 months' supply.

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Health insurance is required for tourist visa applications.
travelInsurance.tips: Medical evacuation coverage is essential, especially for adventure travel (desert camping, mountain hiking, diving). The nearest world-class medical facilities are in Muscat or Dubai.

required: Yellow Fever (if arriving from endemic area)
vaccinations.notes: No special vaccinations required for most travelers. Ensure routine vaccinations are up to date.

waterNotes: Tap water is desalinated and safe in cities. Bottled water recommended in rural areas and for taste. Stay extremely hydrated — Oman is one of the hottest countries on Earth.
foodSafetyTips: Food safety is generally good in hotels and restaurants. Be cautious with street food in summer heat. Fresh seafood is excellent in coastal areas. Stay well-hydrated during desert excursions.
medicalTourismNote: Oman is not a major medical tourism destination. For specialized treatment, patients typically travel to Dubai or India.
metaDescription: Complete health & medication guide for traveling to Oman. Emergency number 9999, strict drug laws, pharmacy tips, vaccination requirements, desert safety advice, and travel insurance information.

hospitals.name: Royal Hospital
hospitals.notes: Oman's largest government hospital. Emergency department. English widely spoken.

hospitals.name: Muscat Private Hospital
hospitals.notes: Leading private hospital. International patient services. Near tourist beach areas.

hospitals.name: Starcare Hospital
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Muscat (Al Khuwair, near Muscat Grand Mall)
hospitals.notes: Modern multi-specialty hospital. Convenient location near hotels.

pharmacyPhrases.english: I need medicine for a headache

dentalCare.availability: Good dental care available in Muscat. Limited outside the capital.
dentalCare.costRange: OMR 15-40 ($39-104) for consultation; OMR 30-100 ($78-260) for fillings
dentalCare.notes: Private dental clinics in Muscat have modern equipment. Many dentists trained in India, UK, or Egypt.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Hospital emergency departments handle urgent dental issues. Book private dental appointments in advance.

mentalHealth.crisisLine: Not widely established — contact Royal Hospital psychiatric department
mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Limited but available in Muscat through private clinics and hospitals.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are developing in Oman. Private hospitals in Muscat offer psychiatric consultations. Cultural sensitivity around mental health is important.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is improving in newer buildings and hotels but remains limited overall, especially in historic areas and desert terrain.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Major hospitals in Muscat are wheelchair accessible.
accessibilityInfo.transport: Limited accessible public transport. Taxis and ride-hailing apps available. Airport assistance provided.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Desert excursions, wadis, and mountain hiking are generally not wheelchair accessible. Newer hotels and malls are accessible. Request ground-floor rooms.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements.
covidStatus.testing: Available at hospitals and clinics in Muscat.
covidStatus.notes: Heat-related illness is the primary health concern. Summer temperatures can exceed 50°C (122°F).

insuranceClaimProcess: Private hospitals may require upfront payment or insurance guarantee. Keep all receipts and medical documentation. Most private hospitals provide English-language reports. File claims with your insurer promptly.
